# Decision record

**Context.** A headers-only analysis of the public Enron email corpus as an engineering case
study: clean the header record, pseudonymize it, look for one change in the communication
network, and measure whether people can be re-identified from what we publish. The corpus is
public; the pipeline is built as if it were not.

## Architecture

Data zones with a path guard per package and an import-boundary test
([docs/architecture.md](architecture.md) has every diagram).

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    Raw[raw archive] --> Ingest[ingest zone<br/>identifiers, purged after run]
    Ingest -->|HMAC pseudonyms| Restricted[restricted zone<br/>pseudonyms only]
    Restricted -->|aggregates meeting k| Release[release<br/>committed]
    Release --> Docs[report, this record, slides]
```

The parser stops at the first blank line of each message, so it cannot reach a body. Every
table crossing a zone is checked against a written contract. Numbers in the documents are
injected from release tables; none is typed.

## Trade-offs

- **Strict content line, including `Subject`.** Content fields (Subject, X-Folder) are never
  stored. We lose threads and reply times and dedupe on sender, second and recipients alone:
  266827 copies removed. Precision and recall are measured in the test suite
  against the synthetic corpus's ground truth; the real corpus has none.
- **Rule-based identity resolution.** Deterministic, explainable rules weighted to precision,
  because a false merge invents a central person while a false split only dilutes one:
  85388 addresses to 84759 entities.
  Missed aliases are the price.
- **Keyed HMAC pseudonyms, and their limit.** Stable for one key, not confirmable by hashing
  guessed addresses. It is still pseudonymization: whoever holds the key can test a candidate,
  and structure re-identifies people. Our own attack on the person-level output (R0)
  re-identified a share of 0.251 of targets for the outsider and
  0.591 for the insider.
- **Aggregates-only release.** So nothing person-level is published. Every cell meets
  k = 5. On the aggregate release (R1) the shares fall to 0 and
  0. With no finding claimed, there is no effect whose loss to measure.

**Finding.** No finding about the crisis year is claimed. H2, H3 passed the pre-registered statistical tests but failed its check against a known artifact of the data (release/artifact_checks.csv): the apparent change is explained by how the data was collected and analysed, not by a detectable change in how people communicated. Every outcome is listed in the report. Among H5–H24, no hypothesis reached the standard to be held true. H16 (share of sent-to contacts who also wrote to the custodian) met its stated rule (median change 0.267, interval 0.144 to 0.386) but fails the retention check: among custodian-to-custodian contacts, whose messages are visible whatever an inbox kept, the change is not established: there the change is 0.111 (interval -0.111 to 0.3). It remains the strongest lead, largely explained by how much inbox mail was kept.

## What changes with real customer data

- **Metadata-only connectors**: request header fields from the mail system, so content never
  leaves the source instead of being skipped after download.
- **Customer-side key custody and an entity registry**: the key and a persisted registry of
  surrogate IDs stay with the customer, so pseudonyms survive changes in identity resolution.
- **Retention**: restricted data expires on a schedule; release tables are re-keyed per release
  so two releases cannot be joined.
- **Works council review** of the questions asked, the minimum group size and the outputs,
  before the first run.
- **Data residency**: processing in the customer's region, with no third-party services.
- **Formal privacy budget**: replace the noise sketch (R2) with differential privacy accounted
  across every published output.

## Not done, and why

- **No finding claimed.** The two apparent crisis-year signals failed checks against known artifacts;
  those checks were added after the first real run and are labelled post hoc.
- **Dropped for time**: the dedupe-rule sensitivity variant.
- **A sketch, not a guarantee**: the noise release (R2) has no formal privacy budget.
- **Identity precision on real data** rests on a manual sample judged by a person, not on ground
  truth. The report lists every limit.
